_comment: The van network layout, as data. Design record and rationale: docs/system-design/network-design.md. Nothing here is derived at runtime except the identity substitution in ssid_template and the radio availability check.

segments.label: Secure
segments._managed_comment: false means the provisioner must never create, renumber or re-bridge this. The Sensa box lives here and the router is reached over it, so touching it cuts the run off from the device it is configuring.

segments.label: IoT
segments._vlan_comment: Not 2. On RutOS switch VLANs 1 and 2 are fixed to LAN and WAN (board.network_options.readonly_vlans), so iot is the one segment whose VLAN ID does not match its third octet. 3 is free on the wire; 192.168.3.0/24 being the Starlink WAN subnet is unrelated, that is a routed network not a switch VLAN.
segments._lan_ports_comment: Physical LAN sockets, by the number printed on the case, that carry this segment untagged. LAN 4 is the wired IoT socket on every van, so a Cerbo GX or a PoE switch for habitation kit plugs in there and lands on iot without any per-van setup.
segments.purpose: Habitation kit, Cerbo GX, ESPHome boards

_wan_comment: 192.168.3.0/24 is the Starlink upstream. It is deliberately not a LAN VLAN and is not listed as a segment. See starlink below.

switch._comment: How the case labels map to switch ports, from the RUTX50 board.json (nomad/tools/probe.json). LAN 1-4 are ports 1-4, the CPU is port 0 and WAN is port 5 on its own read-only VLAN 2. Segments without lan_ports are wireless only and get no switch VLAN. A different model needs its own map here before provisioning; do not guess.

forwarding._comment: Zone to zone. Absent means reject. Return traffic is carried by connection tracking, so HA reaching into iot and cctv needs no reverse entry.

input_policy._comment: Traffic aimed AT the router, which forwarding rules do not constrain at all. Without these, a zone that forwards nowhere can still open the RutOS admin page on its own gateway.

input_exceptions.name: dhcp
input_exceptions.reason: Without this the segment cannot get an address.

input_exceptions.name: dns
input_exceptions.reason: The router is the resolver. Remove this entry if DNS ever moves off it.

zone_exceptions._comment: One port opened between zones that otherwise reject each other. Narrow on purpose: the whole of 'forwarding' above stays as it is.
zone_exceptions.name: sensa_firmware
zone_exceptions.label: Sensa firmware updates
zone_exceptions.reason: Sensa's own devices on iot (Autoterm heaters, fan controller, Van Level) fetch firmware updates from the Sensa App on the box: the install hands them the box's LAN URL on 8099. Without this the download never starts and the install times out (AirD 1.1.1 on a customer box, 2026-10-04). Not pinned to the box's address, which is not in this profile and may change. CAUTION: 8099 is the App's whole API, not only firmware, so every iot device can reach it.

ssids._comment: Not every RUT has a 5 GHz radio. A missing radio is a normal outcome, not a failure.
2.4 GHz only because the kit that joins it is 2.4 GHz only.

ssids._isolation_comment: A radio setting, not a firewall rule. Two clients on one SSID talk through the access point without the traffic ever being routed, so the zone policy does not cover this.

starlink._comment: Selected by the starlink_mode parameter. Both topologies assume the customer has already set the dish up in the Starlink mobile app.
starlink.label: Starlink
starlink._expected_comment: Expected, not guaranteed. docs/devices/starlink-terminal.md records this as not verified on hardware. Read the actual WAN subnet at run time and route via what is really there.
starlink._refuse_comment: Starlink's stock LAN is 192.168.1.0/24, which is exactly the data segment. A router whose WAN and LAN are the same subnet cannot route. Refuse rather than write a broken route; the customer's fix is to change the Starlink LAN in the app.

verify_ports._comment: Reference for the post-run checks, not firewall rules. data reaches iot and cctv wholesale under forwarding above; these are the paths that must actually work afterwards. See docs/system-design/network-design.md section 10.

data_to_iot.reaches: ESPHome discovery sweep, Cerbo Remote Console

iot_to_data.reaches: Sensa App on the box: firmware for Sensa's own devices (zone_exceptions)

scan_subnet._comment: The box works its scan range out from its own address, so it only ever scans the data segment by default. This value must be written to the integration's scan_subnet setting or nothing on the IoT segment is ever discovered.

iot_placement._comment: All habitation IoT lives on the iot segment, including the discovery-fragile infrastructure. That is a deliberate decision for a cleaner security boundary, and it has consequences that are handled here rather than left to fail silently.
iot_placement._reservations_comment: MANDATORY, not advisory. HA sits on the data segment, so name broadcast never reaches it and .local stops resolving for every device on iot. The self-healing described in docs/ip-switch.md does not apply across a segment boundary, so an address change breaks the connection outright. Every device below is pinned by MAC to a fixed address outside the dynamic pool.
iot_placement._reserved_range_comment: Below the DHCP pool start of 50, so the pool can never hand these out. The pool is .50 to .249: a van has few fixed devices (Richard, 2026-11-07).

requires_reservation.reason: Its address is stored inside Z2M's own settings and is deliberately never chased, because changing it automatically risks taking the whole Zigbee network down.
Loses the .local name that survives an address change. Falls back to a pinned IP, which is only safe if the IP cannot move.
Self-heals via the host reconcile loop, so this is belt and braces rather than load bearing.

static_probe_required.reason: mDNS does not cross a segment boundary, so the coordinator is never seen at all. Needs a pinned address. Found by the `http_probe` sweep of `/ha_info` once scan_subnet includes iot, not by a static probe entry.

Address resolution is local to a segment, so the responder answers on 6638 and is then discarded as unidentifiable. The catalog already pins 192.168.2.20 for the dev rig; that pattern becomes the norm.
SSDP does not cross a segment boundary. Sonos also uses multicast between its own speakers, which still works within the segment.

mdns_reflector._comment: A reflector across data and iot would restore name discovery and remove the hard dependency on reservations. It has NOT been established that RutOS ships a usable one. Settle this during the API capability spike; if it exists, the reservations above stay as belt and braces rather than the only thing holding the install together.
